summary: Checked all 20 retained estimates after reading the complete 115628-character markdown, including appendices and references. Extracted the cited PDF pages with pymupdf and checked the numerical cells, column/arm assignments, counts, evaluation procedures, experimental design, exclusions and regression descriptions. All retained statistics match Tables 2, 3, 5, D.4 and D.5. No confirmed numerical, scope or coding error, or missing eligible estimate, was found in the supplied paper. The two script warnings for s1_image_text_hat_vs_hi_no_covariates.se_basis and s1_text_only_hat_vs_hi_no_covariates.se_basis are false positives: extraction-spec.md explicitly permits unclear in both its schema and field notes, and creativity-codebook.md section 10 explicitly defines it. The paper reports session-clustered robust standard errors from random-effects models (PDF p. 8, Table 3; p. 18, Appendix C), but does not unambiguously identify individual versus session allocation or the random-effects grouping. Keeping unclear is justified; these records must not be pooled without clarification. The recorded n_units values 442 and 478 are the printed whole-model observation counts, including all modeled arms, as the extraction notes explain; they are not participant counts or pairwise sample totals. Analysis-specific person counts remain null under the transcribe-only rule. Table 2 SD values are correctly transcribed, with their aggregation level left unresolved. The theme-specific table stars compare human arms with standalone ChatGPT, so withholding them from HAT-versus-HI/HHT contrasts is correct. The separate Training cohort, AI-only and simulated comparisons, subgroup/moderator and mediator analyses, self-reports and models adjusting for major collected in final Questionnaire III are appropriately listed in not_extracted under rules 4-6. No separate supplement is present in the c150 supplement-manifest entry. Independent urllib requests to the Elsevier Article Retrieval API and the article DOI, using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, both failed with WinError 10013. Accordingly, this verification cannot establish completeness of the separately referenced supplementary tables; their unavailability is already documented in the extraction.
